seoTitle: Decking Calculator - Estimate Deck Boards & Materials
metaDescription: Free online Decking Calculator. Figure out exactly how many deck boards, joists, and screws you need to build your custom wooden or composite deck.
secondaryKeywords: how many deck boards do I need
intro: Planning to build a beautiful backyard deck? Our free Decking Calculator tells you exactly how many boards, joists, and fasteners you need, preventing mid-project trips to the lumber yard.
whatIs: The Decking Calculator is a carpentry estimation tool. It takes the overall dimensions of your planned deck and translates them into a highly accurate shopping list of lumber and hardware required for the build.
howToUse: Enter the total length and width of your planned deck.
Select your decking board width (e.g., standard 5.5 inch boards) and length (12ft or 16ft).
Select your joist spacing (usually 16 inches on center).
The tool calculates the total boards, joists, and screws required.
howItWorks: The tool divides the deck width by the board width (plus a standard 1/8 to 1/4 inch gap for drainage) to determine the number of board rows. It then divides the deck length by the board length to calculate total boards, adding a 10% waste factor. Joists are calculated based on the spacing division.
workedExample: A 10x12 foot deck using 12ft boards (5.5in wide). 10 feet = 120 inches. 120 / 5.75 (board + gap) = ~21 boards. Since the boards are exactly the length of the deck, you need exactly 21 boards, plus 2 for waste.
resultInterpretation: The final material list can be taken directly to a hardware store. It ensures you have enough wood to complete the surface, the structural sub-frame, and enough screws to lock it all down.
useCases: DIY Backyard Decks: A homeowner planning a simple ground-level square deck.
Contractor Bidding: A builder quickly estimating the total material cost of composite decking to give a client an accurate quote.
Material Upgrades: Comparing the total board requirement of laying boards straight versus laying them diagonally (which requires more wood and shorter joist spacing).
tipsAndLimitations: Standard 5/4x6 decking boards are actually 5.5 inches wide, not 6 inches. The tool accounts for this 'nominal' vs 'actual' lumber sizing.
If you are installing boards diagonally (at a 45-degree angle), you must increase your waste factor to at least 15%.

faq.question: What is 'on center' joist spacing?
faq.answer: It means measuring from the center of one joist to the center of the next. Standard wood decks use 16-inch spacing. Composite decks often require 12-inch spacing to prevent the boards from sagging.

faq.question: How much of a gap should I leave between boards?
faq.answer: Usually 1/8 to 1/4 inch. This allows water to drain and gives the wood room to naturally expand and contract with the weather.

disclaimer: Tool assumes a standard rectangular layout. Complex decks with multiple levels, stairs, or cutouts will require manual adjustments to the final material list.
